title: Capacity Horizon Advisor and Granular Burst Quota Mapper
author: Aisha Kaur
description: Context: customers running Dedicated fleets reported transient SLA pressure during short spike patterns that are not well-served by the existing autoscaler which focuses on steady-state util signals. This PR introduces the Capacity Horizon Advisor (CHA), a lightweight controller that computes short-term capacity reservations per-tenant based on recent arrival curves and burst risk scores, and a Granular Burst Quota Mapper (GBQM) that exposes per-tenant, timeboxed burst allowances to the serving path. Motivation: reduce tail latency and failed requests during intermittent surges while avoiding long-lived overprovisioning. High level change: 1) CHA service (controller) ingests sampled request timestamps and the utilization sampler to estimate a 1m/5m/15s horizon demand curve, applies an exponential-decay uncertainty model, and outputs a suggested reservation token quota per tenant for the next 60s interval. 2) GBQM maps CHA suggestions to an internal burst-token account per-tenant with soft and hard limits and a decay/return policy; it integrates with the existing token-bucket admission path and emits headroom_curve telemetry. 3) Autoscaler adaptions: the main autoscaler now accepts CHA hints as advisory reservations (configurable via feature flag) and treats them as short-lived soft commitments for prioritization in the warmpool and prewarm steps. 4) Telemetry: new metrics (cha_suggested_tokens, gbqm_active_quota, headroom_curve_p50/p90, cha_confidence) and a small exporter that writes headroom curves to the observability service for slice-by-tenant analysis. 5) Controls: operator knobs added to the dedicated config for horizon window, risk_sensitivity, and decay_rate; sane defaults applied. Design notes: CHA is intentionally advisory—no forced capacity changes without explicit operator opt-in; suggestions are timeboxed and auto-expire to avoid stale reservations. The uncertainty model penalizes suggestions that require >20% short-term cluster commitment and gradually downgrades suggestions when system-wide spare capacity is low. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag "cha.enabled" default false; canary rollout to a single warmpool in us-west-2 serving low-volume tenants; monitor headroom_curve and p99 latency for 72h; expand to additional pools on green signals. Migration: no customer migrations needed; default behavior unchanged until flag enabled by SRE. Backwards compatibility: GBQM integrates with token-bucket admission via an additive allowance path and falls back to preexisting admission logic when disabled. Testing: unit tests for the uncertainty model and mapper rules, integration test harness simulating spike patterns, and a perf canary run in benchmark-lab showing a 35-60% reduction in spike-induced dropped requests for a synthetic 10x short burst workload with <3% steady-state cost increase. Security: no new exfiltration paths; suggestions are internal-only and logged at debug level. Observability and alerting: new dashboard panels and alerts added for anomalous suggestion rates and suggestions rejected due to cluster constraints. Safety: CHA suggestions are capped by per-tenant max_quota and global soft_budget to avoid capacity starvation. Implementation files: controller implementation in controllers/cha/ (Go), GBQM admission in serving/admission/burst_mapper.go, autoscaler hook in autoscaler/hints_consumer.go, metrics/exporter in telemetry/cha_exporter.go, Helm values patch for dedicated, and documentation. Performance: bench runs on a 200-node dedicated test cluster indicate steady-state 0.5–2% CPU overhead and memory footprint +12MB per CHA replica; latency improvement primarily visible at p95-p999 during bursts. CI: runs unit/integration/lint and a short canary scenario; all checks passed after a flaky test fix. See commits and changed files below for exact diffs.
